Formatting a post for Instant View

By Dana Writer

Every blog post carries more than words: strong, emphasis, struck, inline() and a relative link that must survive the trip. This paragraph is deliberately long enough to give Readability something to score, because a page under four hundred characters is a link card, not an article.

Headings keep their rank

The page uses every heading level: h2, h3, h4, h5 and h6 all appear below so the converter must map six levels onto Telegra.ph's two. Nothing may leak as bare text between blocks.

Third level

Third-level text sits under the third heading.

Fourth level

Fourth-level text sits under the fourth heading.

Fifth level

Fifth-level text sits under the fifth heading.

Sixth level

Sixth-level text sits under the sixth heading.

Code

Inline code such as npm test stays monospace.

function greet(name) {
  const message = `hello ${name}`;
  return message;
}
